summary: Two corrections after the membership thread resolved. First, a consistency fix: the removed-member question now has a final refuting interpretation, so its disposition is set to explained. Second, I bounded a remaining premise of the asserted retry-growth defect - whether the retained read state can outlive the process. Source trace shows it cannot: newRaft builds the read state fresh (readOnly via newReadOnly at raft.go:462, pendingReadIndexMessages a nil slice field at raft.go:430-435), the only mutations are the stepLeader append and the release-path swap, and the Storage interface exposes no read-state member (storage.go:48-95, with no ReadState/readStates reference in storage.go or raftpb). So a restart starts with an empty queue and empty ack map, making the accumulation process-lifetime-bounded and giving operators an incidental remedy. I recorded that as a durable fact and added it to the interpretation as a severity bound, not a defence: within a lifetime the library still imposes no limit and reclaims nothing, retained payload still equals accepted requests times caller-chosen context size, and the per-request heartbeat plus release burst are unchanged. Receipt, decisive indices and the asserted claim are untouched, and the previously stated boundaries (CheckQuorum false required for unlimited growth, modelled triggers, unmeasured footprint/OOM/liveness) remain.
